html:
The Kolla, or Coya, are an Indigenous people of the high, dry puna of northwest Argentina, in Jujuy and Salta, and of nearby Bolivia. The name comes from Qullasuyu, the southern quarter of the Inca Empire, which reached this area in the late 1400s.

The peoples of the area, such as the Omaguaca and Atacameño, herded llamas and farmed potatoes and quinoa in the high valleys. Under Spanish rule they worked on haciendas and in mines, and many came to speak Quechua and Spanish. In 1946 Kolla people walked about 2,000 kilometres to Buenos Aires to demand their land back, a march called the Malón de la Paz. They remain one of the largest Indigenous peoples of Argentina.
